A.reason: All candidates are feasible using notes and calendars, preserve voluntary acceptance, and compare completion, rework and burden. Candidates 0 and 7 share the consent-based queue mechanism; explicit dispositions repair its exception handling rather than create a new mechanism. The other groups use rotating coordination, meeting-time execution, standing delegation, prerequisite readiness, early sample review, backup recovery and advance artifacts. Candidate 7 best combines broad applicability, bounded meeting time, explicit ownership and deadlines, voluntary handoffs, and inspectable handling of unfinished work without chair chasing.

B.reason: All candidates satisfy the hard constraints without a definite serious violation. Their primary mechanisms are voluntary commitment, rotating coordination, immediate execution, delegated authority, calendar scheduling, backup continuity and recipient verification. Candidate 0 provides the strongest general-purpose foundation: explicit acceptance, bounded commitments, visible unclaimed work, owner updates and a comparison that measures original-deadline completion, rework and individual administrative burden. The alternatives depend more on particular causes of stalled work.

pair.reason: A7 modestly improves on B0 by specifying dispositions for overdue and withdrawn commitments, voluntary handoffs, absent-owner handling and a fallback when no recorder volunteers. These practical repairs reduce ambiguity that could otherwise restore chair chasing. Both are lightweight and inspectable; B0 specifies the rework observation window more clearly.
